context: Add username-shaped parts (user, username, login) to _SECRET_KEY_PARTS, or introduce an explicit connection-identity key class if usernames should be recorded for some platforms and not others - decide which, because a username is identifying rather than strictly secret and some adapters may legitimately want it in provenance. Guard against over-redaction the way #1346 did: 'user' as a substring would also catch e.g. 'user_agent' or 'num_users', so prefer bounded matching plus a non-credential guard test. Once shared redaction covers it, DuckLake's adapter-local _CREDENTIAL_CONFIG_KEYS scrub can be reduced or removed.
description: is_secret_option_key() in benchbox/core/results/platform_options.py does not match user/username/pg_user/http_user/login/account, so any adapter carrying a username in platform_config exports it verbatim in platform_raw_config. VERIFIED on a non-DuckLake adapter 2026-07-30: PostgreSQLAdapter(username='alice-sentinel', password='hunter2-sentinel') normalized metadata contains username='alice-sentinel' while password is correctly '<redacted>'. This affects every PG-family, Redshift, Snowflake, Trino and similar adapter. PR #1364 fixed it for DuckLake ONLY, by scrubbing an explicit key set in the adapter's own get_normalized_result_metadata override - a local patch on a repo-wide problem. Fourth instance of the same family found in this effort (#1333 ATTACH error, #1345 MotherDuck traceback, #1346 *_key_id export, #1364 pg_user): key-NAME-based redaction keeps missing things because it only protects keys whose names happen to match.

preserves.behavior: Already-redacted keys (password/token/secret/key_id/...) keep their current behavior
Non-credential option keys still export their real values

verifications.description: A connection username is redacted in sanitized platform options
verifications.expected: all pass; new case asserts REDACTED_VALUE for username/pg_user and real values for non-credential keys

work_units.summary: Decide and implement how username-shaped keys are treated
Tests for username redaction plus an over-redaction guard
